    --probe-copy-prefill               MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-copy-prefill --model-dir <EXL3 pack> [--prompt-ids <file>] [--probe-copy-prefill-n N] [--prefill-chunk C]: the prompt's greedy decode continuation of N tokens is offered as a copy to the --copy-span-prefill step; checks that the step's choices and committed state are bit-identical to the same tokens read as prompt (RESULT: COPY_PREFILL_EXACT | COPY_PREFILL_MISMATCH) and reports how many positions the prompt-reading path chooses differently from the decoding path, with their logit margins  [off] (per box)
    --probe-copy-prefill-break <N>     --probe-copy-prefill: K >= 1 replaces copied token K by another id, so the step must stop by row K-1 and exercise its roll-back and re-run (0 = off: the copy is the exact decode continuation)  [0] (per box)
    --probe-copy-prefill-n <N>         --probe-copy-prefill: copied tokens offered to the step (the stretch is N+1 prefill rows)  [256] (per box)
    --probe-copy-span-replay           MODE (no model, no GPU): replay the copy-span proposer round by round along recorded outputs (--ids-file) and print per-record and total rounds with a proposal, tokens they emitted, rounds with zero accepted and fully accepted rounds; honours --copy-span-min-n / --copy-span-max-w / --copy-span-start-w  [off] (per box)
    --probe-dense-resident             MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-dense-resident --model-dir <EXL3 pack> --prompt-ids <file> [--prefill-chunk C]: prefills the prompt with the per-pass dense decode and with --exl3-dense-resident's kept matrices and compares recurrent state, trunk KV and the first token bit for bit (RESULT: DENSE_RESIDENT_EXACT | DENSE_RESIDENT_MISMATCH)  [off] (per box)
    --probe-exl3-packpf                MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-exl3-packpf --model-dir <EXL3 pack> [--packpf-lens 1240,1180,1120] [--packpf-chunk 2048] [--packpf-reps 3] [--max-seq-len N]: prefills K prompts one by one (the served chunk grid) and in packed passes (pass k = chunk k of every prompt), compares every recurrent state, KV, QSA and head-fill byte and the seam logits bit for bit, and times both (RESULT: PACKPF_EXACT | PACKPF_MISMATCH)  [off] (per box)
    --probe-gpu-wait                   MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-gpu-wait [--gpu-wait spin|hybrid|block] [--probe-gpu-wait-mib 1024,16] [--probe-gpu-wait-reps 200]: per wait of an async memset of each size, the GPU time, wall time, wake-up overhead and the waiting thread's CPU time under the resolved --gpu-wait policy (GPU_WAIT_PROBE lines)  [off] (per box)
    --probe-gpu-wait-mib <TEXT>        --probe-gpu-wait: memset sizes in MiB, comma-separated (1024 ~ a 5 ms wait, 16 ~ 0.1 ms)  [1024,16] (per box)
    --probe-gpu-wait-reps <N>          --probe-gpu-wait: timed waits per size (after 5 warm-up waits; medians reported)  [200] (per box)
    --probe-lane-wide-cost             MODE (GPU, one box, timing only): --probe-lane-wide-cost --model-dir <EXL3 pack> --prompt-ids <file> [--probe-lane-wide-rows 16,32,64] [--probe-lane-wide-reps 7]: 16 slots read the prompt, then the median times of a prefill-class chunk of R rows and its lm_head judge, the decode-class step over 1..16 distinct slots and one lane's draft chain of 1..6 drafts  [off] (per box)
    --probe-lane-wide-pin              MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-lane-wide-pin --model-dir <EXL3 pack> [--probe-lane-wide-reps N]: the wide pass's small fp16 projections (hc down / up, GDN a / b, PLE key / value) through cuBLASLt with the algo pinned to the 160-row plan: bit-identity of every row at every row count and offset against the 160-row call (RESULT: WIDE_PIN_EXACT | WIDE_PIN_MISMATCH), then the time per call: tail GEMM vs cuBLASLt's own plan vs the pinned plan  [off] (per box)
    --probe-lane-wide-reps <N>         --probe-lane-wide-cost: timed repetitions per cell (after two warm runs)  [7] (per box)
    --probe-lane-wide-rows <TEXT>      --probe-lane-wide-cost: the chunk row counts timed (comma-separated)  [16,32,64,96,128,176] (per box)
    --probe-lane-wide-xclass           MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-lane-wide-xclass --model-dir <EXL3 pack> --prompt-ids <JSON list of prompt id lists> [--probe-lane-wide-rows S]: the wide verify of lane 0 (one segment, then inside a pass with every other prompt as a segment), with --exl3-mid-gemm off and on, against the token-by-token decode-class ground truth: per row logits rel-L2, argmax agreement, the ground truth's top-2 margin, and whether the lane's rows depend on the rest of the pass  [off] (per box)
    --probe-mid-gemm                   MODE (GPU, one box): --probe-mid-gemm --model-dir <EXL3 pack> [--probe-lane-wide-rows ..] [--probe-lane-wide-reps N]: every dense trunk matrix through --exl3-mid-gemm: bit-identity with the decode-class chain and row-independence (RESULT: MID_GEMM_EXACT | MID_GEMM_MISMATCH), then the per-pass dense time at each row count against the kept fp16 and the reconstruct arms  [off] (per box)
    --psk-xcheck                       PSK eager cross-check  [off]
    --qsa-dump                         NVFP4 QSA dumps  [off]
    --qsa-dump-layer <N>               EXL3 QSA dump layer  [unset]
    --qsa-rowdump-layer <N>            EXL3 QSA row dump layer  [unset]
    --qsa-time                         QSA timing (syncs)  [off]
    --regime-csv <PATH>                --probe-exl3-regime: per-step CSV (bit differences, max |dlogit|, rel-L2, KL, top-1 agreement, margin)  [unset] (per box)
    --regime-joiner <PATH>             --probe-exl3-regime: the long (joiner) prompt, past the sparse-attention switch (2,051 tokens on Flash-Next)  [unset] (per box)
    --regime-order <short-first|long-first>
                                       --probe-exl3-regime: row order inside the mixed step (runner row first, or the joiner row first)  [short-first] (per box)
    --regime-runner <PATH>             --probe-exl3-regime: the short (runner) prompt, raw text or a JSON token-id array  [unset] (per box)
    --regime-steps <N>                 --probe-exl3-regime: teacher-forced decode steps  [1600] (per box)
    --regime-time <N>                  --probe-exl3-regime: after the comparison loop, time N served 4-row mixed decode steps (three rows at/below the sparse switch + the joiner); with --regime-steps 0 this is all the probe does  [0] (per box)
    --reprime-xcheck                   re-prime eager cross-check  [off]
    --round-trace                      DFlash2 round trace; EXL3 server: each request's [mtp-stats] line also carries seed= and arms= (one entry per round: P = packed verify, S = lone speculative verify, c = control round, p = plain step, each followed by the tokens it produced; the first 48 rounds) and toks= (the ids of its first 8 generated tokens)  [off]
    --sched-trace                      EXL3 server, diagnostic: one [sched-trace] line per scheduler step (wall time, the arm that served it, each busy request's tokens, position and thinking/answer phase) and per prefill chunk (slot, rows, ms), each stamped with the wall clock; for laying out where the time of concurrent requests goes. Output and speed are unchanged apart from the log lines  [off] (per box)
    --sel-union-stats                  EXL3 prefill, diagnostic: on the first three chunks with >= 1,024 sparse rows, print SEL_UNION lines: how many distinct keys groups of 2..32 neighbouring query rows select (the K/V bytes a union-staged gather would read). Adds host copies; output unchanged  [off] (per box)
    --spec-mode <drafter|oracle|miss|adapt|mixed|sampled|chi>
                                       Naive --probe-naive-spec mode: drafter | oracle | miss | adapt | mixed | sampled | chi  [drafter] (per box)
    --spec-pass-xcheck                 spec-pass eager cross-check  [off]
    --step-topk-dir <PATH>             EXL3 step top-k dump dir  [unset]
    --tool-trace <PATH>                server (TOOLEVAL): append one JSON line per tool-involved chat turn (the request offers tools, or its history carries a tool result) to this file: the tail of the rendered prompt, the model's raw output (thinking included), the text the tool parser was given, and the parsed verdict (content, tool_calls, finish) with the request class (stream, seed, sampling, thinking, tool count). Off by default; zero cost when off. The lines are prompt and model output: treat the file as user data  [off]
    --tp-accept <N>                    TP bench_accept depth (set = run the accept branch)  [unset]
    --tp-agree-drill <N>               test drill, NVFP4 packs, one-sided (per box: it acts on the box whose command line carries it): corrupt THIS rank's agree hash at scheduler step N, once per head session (a resident node supervisor started with this flag re-arms it for every head that connects; the corruption depends on the rank, so a drill armed on two ranks cannot cancel). Inert, with a boot line saying so, on EXL3 packs (use --tp-width-drill) and at TP=1  [unset] (per box)

The lie depends on the rank, so a drill armed on two ranks is still caught. A boot line says the drill is armed, or why it is inert (NVFP4 pack, TP=1, N <= rank)  [unset] (per box)

    --world <value>
    --wp16-b-ids <value>
    --wp16-split <value>
    --x-in <value>
    --xport
    --xtp-gates <value>
    --xtp-gen <value>
    --xtp-ident-only
    --xtp-out <value>
    --xtp-pf-chunk <value>
    --xtp-ref <value>
    --xtp-sp-fault <value>
    --xtp-time <value>
    --y-out <value>

  A value that really starts with "--" must be written --option=value; a value-taking option is never taken from the next --flag - no value-taking option, registry or hand-read, ever eats one (F7/F9).
